title: In the future
scope: The future tense (बोलूँगा, बोलेगी, बोलोगे, बोलेंगे) and the irregular futures of होना, लेना, देना, with vowel shortening (पिएगा); the future continuous (जा रहा होगा) and the presumptive future (“must be”: वह दफ़्तर में होगा, पढ़ती होगी); emphatic ही and its coalesced forms (यही, वही, इसी, उसी, यहीं, वहीं, अभी, सभी, हमीं); expressions of quantity (बहुत-सा/-सी/-से, -सा “-ish”, कम, ज़्यादा, कम से कम, ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा, थोड़ा-बहुत, काफ़ी); the infinitive as verbal noun: subject, oblique before postpositions (जाने से पहले, पहुँचने पर), purpose, लायक़/योग्य “worth …ing”, and with आना “know how to”

vocab.en: for this very reason, that's why

gloss.ही: emphasises or limits the word before it (“only”, “very”, “right”); often no single English word

items.q: Fill the gap: “I will go to Delhi tomorrow morning. (a man speaking)”
items.en: I[0] {will go}[4] to Delhi[3] {tomorrow morning}[1+2]. (a man speaking)
wrong: जाऊँगी is feminine. The speaker is a man.
जाएगा goes with तू, यह and वह. मैं takes -ū̃gā: जाऊँगा.
Not a word: मैं takes -ū̃gā or -ū̃gī, never a plural ending.
items.why: The future adds -ū̃gā to the stem for मैं, -egā for तू, यह, वह, -oge for तुम and -ẽge for हम, आप, ये, वे. Feminine forms end in -ī: -ū̃gī, -egī, -ogī, -ẽgī.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita will write a letter in the evening.”
items.say: सीता शाम को एक चिट्ठी लिखेगी ।
items.en: Sita[0] {will write}[5] a[3] letter[4] {in the evening}[1+2].
wrong: लिखेगा is masculine. Sita is a woman.
लिखेंगी is plural. Sita, spoken of plainly, takes the singular.
items.why: वह, यह and a singular noun take -egā (m) or -egī (f).

items.q: Fill the gap: “At what time will you come tomorrow?”
items.say: तुम लोग कल किस समय आओगे ?
items.en: {At what time}[3+4] will you[0+1] come[5] tomorrow[2]?
wrong: -ẽge goes with हम, आप, ये and वे. तुम takes -oge: आओगे.
Not a word: तुम always takes plural agreement, -oge (or -ogī).
items.why: तुम — आओगे (to men or a mixed group), आओगी (to women).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Will you come to our house tomorrow?”
items.say: क्या आप कल हमारे घर आएँगे ?
items.en: Will you[1] come[5] to our[3] house[4] tomorrow[2]?
wrong: आओगे goes with तुम. आप takes -ẽge: आएँगे.
आएगा is singular. आप always takes plural agreement.
items.why: After a vowel stem the endings are spelled with a full vowel letter, as in आएगा, आएँगे.

items.q: Put it in the future
wrong: सीखती होगी is the presumptive: “Pinki must be learning the tabla”. The simple future is one word, सीखेगी.
सीखेगा is masculine. Pinki is a girl.
items.why: The future has no separate auxiliary: सीखती है becomes सीखेगी.
items.en: Pinki[0] {will learn}[2] the tabla[1].

items.q: Fill the gap: “I will buy all the vegetables today. (a woman speaking)”
items.en: I[0] {will buy}[4] all[2] the vegetables[3] today[1]. (a woman speaking)
wrong: ख़रीदूँगा is masculine. The speaker is a woman.
ख़रीदेगी goes with वह or यह. मैं takes -ū̃gī.
items.why: The future adds -ū̃gā to the stem for मैं, -egā for तू, यह, वह, -oge for तुम and -ẽge for हम, आप, ये, वे. Feminine forms end in -ī: -ū̃gī, -egī, -ogī, -ẽgī.

items.q: Which means “Mohan won't come today”?
wrong: आता is the imperfective: a habit, “doesn't come”. “Won't come” is the future, आएगा.
आएगी is feminine. Mohan is a man.
items.why: नहीं goes before the future verb, which needs no auxiliary.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Will you eat this food? (to तू, a boy)”
items.en: Will you[0] eat[3] this[1] food[2]? (to तू, a boy)
wrong: खाओगे goes with तुम. तू takes the singular, -egā.
items.why: तू takes the same endings as वह — खाएगा, खाएगी.

items.q: Fill the gap: “They will return from Lucknow tomorrow.”
items.say: वे लोग कल लखनऊ से लौटेंगे ।
items.en: They[0+1] {will return}[5] from[4] Lucknow[3] tomorrow[2].
wrong: लौटेगा is singular. वे लोग is plural.
items.why: The future adds -ū̃gā to the stem for मैं, -egā for तू, यह, वह, -oge for तुम and -ẽge for हम, आप, ये, वे. Feminine forms end in -ī: -ū̃gī, -egī, -ogī, -ẽgī.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I will give you the money tomorrow. (a man speaking)”
items.en: I[0] {will give}[4] you[1] the money[3] tomorrow[2]. (a man speaking)
wrong: Not a word: देना is irregular, and the stem vowel drops: दूँगा.
दूँगी is feminine. The speaker is a man.
items.why: होना, लेना and देना are irregular: हूँगा, होगा, होगे, होंगे — लूँगा, लेगी, लेंगे — दूँगा, देगा, देंगे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Which sari will you take? (to a woman)”
items.en: Which[1] sari[2] will you[0] take[3]? (to a woman)
wrong: Not a word: लेना is irregular, लेगी, लेंगी. And आप takes the plural.
लेंगे is masculine. This is asked of a woman.
items.why: होना, लेना and देना are irregular: हूँगा, होगा, होगे, होंगे — लूँगा, लेगी, लेंगे — दूँगा, देगा, देंगे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Tomorrow it will be very hot.”
items.en: Tomorrow[0] {it will be}[3] very[1] hot[2].
wrong: होगा is masculine. The verb agrees with गर्मी, which is feminine.
होंगी is plural. गर्मी is singular.
items.why: होना — होगा, होगी (singular); होंगे, होंगी (plural).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Will you be at home tomorrow? (to a man)”
items.en: Will you[0] be[4] {at home}[2+3] tomorrow[1]? (to a man)
wrong: होंगे goes with हम, आप, ये, वे. तुम takes होगे.
होगा is singular. तुम always takes plural agreement.
items.why: होना, लेना and देना are irregular: हूँगा, होगा, होगे, होंगे — लूँगा, लेगी, लेंगे — दूँगा, देगा, देंगे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I will take only one samosa. (a woman speaking)”
items.en: I[0] {will take}[4] only[1] one[2] samosa[3]. (a woman speaking)
wrong: लूँगा is masculine. The speaker is a woman.
लेगी goes with वह or यह. मैं takes लूँगी.
items.why: होना, लेना and देना are irregular: हूँगा, होगा, होगे, होंगे — लूँगा, लेगी, लेंगे — दूँगा, देगा, देंगे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The child won't drink cold milk.”
items.en: {The child}[0] {won't drink}[3+4] cold[1] milk[2].
wrong: पीता is the imperfective, “doesn't drink” as a habit. “Won't drink” is the future.
पिएगी is feminine. बच्चा is masculine.
items.why: Stems in -ī and -ū shorten the vowel in the future: पीना → पिएगा, छूना → छुएगा.

items.q: What is the future of छूना with वह (a man)?
wrong: छूता is the imperfective participle, not the future.
छुऊँगा is the मैं form. वह takes -egā.
items.why: छूना shortens ū to u in the future: छुएगा.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I will be in the office at ten o'clock. (a man speaking)”
items.say: मैं दस बजे दफ़्तर में हूँगा ।
items.en: I[0] {will be}[5] in[4] the office[3] {at ten o'clock}[1+2]. (a man speaking)
wrong: होगा goes with तू, यह and वह. मैं takes हूँगा.
हूँगी is feminine. The speaker is a man.
items.why: होना, लेना and देना are irregular: हूँगा, होगा, होगे, होंगे — लूँगा, लेगी, लेंगे — दूँगा, देगा, देंगे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “At this time tomorrow I will be going to Lucknow. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: कल इस समय मैं लखनऊ जा रहा ___ ।
items.say: कल इस समय मैं लखनऊ जा रहा हूँगा ।
items.en: {At this time}[1+2] tomorrow[0] I[3] {will be going}[5+6+7] to Lucknow[4]. (a man speaking)
wrong: हूँ is present: “I am going”. “Will be going” needs the future auxiliary, हूँगा.
होगा goes with वह. मैं takes हूँगा.
items.why: The future continuous is the stem + रहा, रही, रहे + the future of होना.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Next year my daughter will be studying in London.”
items.hi: अगले साल मेरी बेटी लंदन में पढ़ रही ___ ।
items.say: अगले साल मेरी बेटी लंदन में पढ़ रही होगी ।
items.en: {Next year}[0+1] my[2] daughter[3] {will be studying}[6+7+8] in[5] London[4].
wrong: होगा is masculine. बेटी is feminine.
items.why: पढ़ रही होगी “will be studying”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj must be in the office now.”
items.en: Raj[0] {must be}[4] in[3] the office[2] now[1].
wrong: है states a fact: “Raj is in the office”. “Must be” is an assumption, which the future expresses.
items.why: The future of होना can make an assumption about the present: “must be”. It may follow a continuous (जा रहा होगा) or an imperfective participle (जाता होगा).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mother must be working in the garden right now.”
items.hi: माँ अभी बग़ीचे में काम कर रही ___ ।
items.say: माँ अभी बग़ीचे में काम कर रही होंगी ।
items.en: Mother[0] {must be working}[4+5+6+7] in[3] the garden[2] {right now}[1].
wrong: होंगे is masculine. Respect makes Mother's auxiliary plural, but it stays feminine.
items.why: The future of होना can make an assumption about the present: “must be”. It may follow a continuous (जा रहा होगा) or an imperfective participle (जाता होगा).

items.q: Fill the gap: “That girl presumably studies at our school.”
items.hi: वह लड़की हमारे स्कूल में पढ़ती ___ ।
items.say: वह लड़की हमारे स्कूल में पढ़ती होगी ।
items.en: That[0] girl[1] {presumably studies}[5+6] at[4] our[2] school[3].
wrong: होगा is masculine. लड़की is feminine.
है states a fact: “studies”. “Presumably” is an assumption: पढ़ती होगी.
items.why: The imperfective participle + होगा makes an assumption about a habit or state.

items.q: Make it an assumption (“must be …ing”)
wrong: लिखेगी is the simple future, “Sita will write”. “Must be writing” keeps रही and puts the auxiliary in the future.
होगा is masculine. Sita is a woman.
items.why: है becomes होगी — रही stays.
items.en: Sita[0] {must be writing}[2+3+4] a letter[1].

items.q: In वह अभी दफ़्तर में होगा, what does होगा express?
items.a: An assumption about the present: “he must be in the office now”
wrong: A future event: “he will be in the office”
अभी “now” shows that the speaker means the present. Without it, होगा could also be future.
A past habit would be the imperfective with था.
items.why: The future of होना can make an assumption about the present: “must be”. It may follow a continuous (जा रहा होगा) or an imperfective participle (जाता होगा).

items.q: Fill the gap: “At this time tomorrow Pratap will be on the plane.”
items.hi: प्रताप कल इस समय हवाई जहाज़ में ___ ।
items.say: प्रताप कल इस समय हवाई जहाज़ में होगा ।
items.en: {At this time}[2+3] tomorrow[1] Pratap[0] {will be}[7] on[6] the plane[4+5].
wrong: होंगे is plural. Pratap, spoken of plainly, takes होगा.
था is past: “was”. कल with the future means “tomorrow”.
items.why: कल is “yesterday” or “tomorrow”; the tense decides.

lessons.title: ही, यही, यहीं
lessons.desc: Emphatic ही and its special forms

items.q: Fill the gap: “Only I will do this work. (a man speaking)”
items.en: {Only I}[0+1] {will do}[4] this[2] work[3]. (a man speaking)
wrong: भी means “also”: “I too will do this work”.
तो sets मैं against others (“as for me”). “Only” is ही.
items.why: ही emphasises or limits the word just before it, often “only”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My office is right here.”
items.en: My[0] office[1] is[3] {right here}[2].
wrong: यही is यह + ही, “this very one”. “Right here” is यहीं, with the nasal.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I like this very sari.”
items.en: I[0] like[3+4] {this very}[1] sari[2].
wrong: यहीं is “right here”, a place. “This very” is यही.
वही is “that very one, the same”.
items.why: यह + ही = यही, वह + ही = वही.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We will return that same day.”
items.en: We[0] {will return}[3] {that same}[1] day[2].
wrong: उसे is उस को, “to him, her, it”. A time phrase needs the oblique उस + ही — उसी दिन.
वही is direct. A time phrase is oblique: उसी दिन.
items.why: उस + ही = उसी, इस + ही = इसी.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I have only two hours.”
items.say: मेरे पास दो ही घंटे हैं ।
items.en: I[0+1] have[5] only[3] two[2] hours[4].
wrong: सिर्फ़ goes before what it limits: सिर्फ़ दो घंटे. ही follows it: दो ही घंटे.
items.why: ही emphasises or limits the word just before it, often “only”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Pinki is coming right now.”
items.en: Pinki[0] {is coming}[2+3+4] {right now}[1].
wrong: यहीं is “right here”, a place, not a time.
items.why: अब + ही = अभी “right now”.

items.q: What does हम + ही become?
wrong: Not a word: हम + ही coalesces to हमीं.
items.why: Some pronouns coalesce with ही — मुझी, हमीं, उसी, उन्हीं.

items.q: What does उन + ही become?
wrong: Not a word: उन + ही is written उन्हीं.
items.why: उन + ही = उन्हीं, इन + ही = इन्हीं, तुम + ही = तुम्हीं.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This is the same shop.”
items.en: This[0] is[3] {the same}[1] shop[2].
wrong: यह वह दुकान है is just “this is that shop”. “The same” needs ही — वही.
items.why: वही and उसी also mean “the same”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan is ill; that's why he won't come today.”
items.hi: मोहन बीमार है, ___ लिए वह आज नहीं आएगा ।
items.say: मोहन बीमार है, इसी लिए वह आज नहीं आएगा ।
items.en: Mohan[0] is[2] ill[1]; {that's why}[3+4] he[5] won't[7] come[8] today[6].
wrong: यही is direct. Before लिए the pronoun is oblique: इसी लिए.
items.why: इसी लिए “for this very reason, that's why” is more emphatic than इस लिए “so”.

items.q: Which means “Only Sita knows Gujarati”?
wrong: ही limits the word before it, here गुजराती — “Sita knows only Gujarati”.
items.why: ही follows the word it limits and does not change its case.

lessons.title: बहुत-सी, कम से कम
lessons.desc: Many, little, at least, at most

items.q: Fill the gap: “I have many saris. (a woman speaking)”
items.en: I[0+1] have[4] many[2] saris[3]. (a woman speaking)
wrong: -sā agrees like an adjective. साड़ियाँ is feminine: बहुत-सी.
बहुत-से is masculine. साड़ियाँ is feminine.
items.why: बहुत-सा, -sī, -se “many, a lot of” agrees with its noun.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There were many people in the market.”
items.en: {There were}[4] many[2] people[3] in[1] the market[0].
wrong: बहुत-सी is feminine. लोग is masculine plural.
बहुत-सा is singular. लोग is plural.
items.why: बहुत-से लोग “many people”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “His kurta is reddish.”
items.en: His[0] kurta[1] is[3] reddish[2].
wrong: लाल-सी is feminine. कुरता is masculine.
लाल-से is plural. कुरता is singular.
items.why: -sā after an adjective gives an “-ish” sense and agrees like an -ā adjective.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Very few people live in this village.”
items.hi: इस गाँव में बहुत ___ लोग रहते हैं ।
items.say: इस गाँव में बहुत कम लोग रहते हैं ।
items.en: {Very few}[3+4] people[5] live[6+7] in[2] this[0] village[1].
wrong: बहुत ज़्यादा is “very many, too many”.
कम से कम is “at least”, and needs a number after it.
items.why: कम “little, few, less” and ज़्यादा “much, many, more” are both adjectives and adverbs.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I need at least two hours.”
items.say: मुझे कम से कम दो घंटे चाहिए ।
items.en: I[0] need[6] {at least}[1+2+3] two[4] hours[5].
items.why: कम से कम “at least”; ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा and अधिक से अधिक “at most”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I will eat at most five samosas. (a man speaking)”
items.say: मैं ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा पाँच समोसे खाऊँगा ।
items.en: I[0] {will eat}[6] {at most}[1+2+3] five[4] samosas[5]. (a man speaking)
wrong: बहुत-से is “many”, and does not go with a number.
items.why: ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा “at most”.

items.q: Which means “many big houses”?
wrong: Here बहुत qualifies बड़े — “very big houses”.
बहुत-सा बड़ा मकान is singular: “a lot of big house”.
items.why: -se after बहुत shows that it qualifies the noun, not the adjective.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I have a certain amount of money.”
items.en: I[0+1] have[4] {a certain amount of}[2] money[3].
wrong: बहुत-सा पैसा is “a lot of money”.
कम से कम is “at least”, and needs a quantity after it.
items.why: थोड़ा-बहुत “a certain amount, some”.

lessons.title: जाने से पहले
lessons.desc: The infinitive as a noun: “going”, “to go”

items.q: Fill the gap: “Living alone is difficult.”
items.en: Living[1] alone[0] is[3] difficult[2].
wrong: रहने is the oblique, used before a postposition or for purpose. As a subject the infinitive is direct.
रहता is the imperfective participle. “Living” as a subject is the infinitive, रहना.
Not a word: the oblique infinitive ends in -ne, with no nasal.
items.why: The infinitive is also a masculine noun: direct as a subject (जाना), oblique in -e before a postposition or for purpose (जाने).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Wash your hands before eating. (to तुम)”
items.say: खाना खाने से पहले हाथ धोओ ।
items.en: Wash[5] {your hands}[4] before[2+3] eating[0+1]. (to तुम)
wrong: Before a postposition the infinitive is oblique: खाने से पहले.
Not a word: the oblique infinitive ends in -ne, with no nasal.
items.why: The infinitive is also a masculine noun: direct as a subject (जाना), oblique in -e before a postposition or for purpose (जाने).

items.q: Fill the gap: “On reaching the office I drink tea. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: दफ़्तर ___ पर मैं चाय पीता हूँ ।
items.say: दफ़्तर पहुँचने पर मैं चाय पीता हूँ ।
items.en: {On reaching}[1+2] the office[0] I[3] drink[5+6] tea[4]. (a man speaking)
wrong: Before पर the infinitive is oblique: पहुँचने पर.
पहुँचते is the imperfective participle. “On reaching” is the oblique infinitive + पर.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + पर “on …ing”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children are going to play in the garden.”
items.hi: बच्चे बग़ीचे में ___ जा रहे हैं ।
items.say: बच्चे बग़ीचे में खेलने जा रहे हैं ।
items.en: {The children}[0] {are going}[4+5+6] to play[3] in[2] the garden[1].
wrong: For purpose the infinitive is oblique: खेलने जा रहे हैं.
Not a word: the oblique infinitive ends in -ne, with no nasal.
items.why: The oblique infinitive on its own can express purpose, “in order to”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I am going to the post office to send this letter. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: मैं यह चिट्ठी भेजने के ___ डाकघर जा रहा हूँ ।
items.say: मैं यह चिट्ठी भेजने के लिए डाकघर जा रहा हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] {am going}[7+8+9] {to the post office}[6] to send[3+4+5] this[1] letter[2]. (a man speaking)
items.why: Purpose: the oblique infinitive alone, or followed by के लिए or को.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Her songs are worth listening to.”
items.en: Her[0] songs[1] are[4] worth[3] {listening to}[2].
wrong: Before लायक़ the infinitive is oblique: सुनने लायक़.
सुनता is the imperfective participle. “Worth …ing” is the oblique infinitive + लायक़.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + (के) लायक़ or योग्य “worth …ing”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My daughter can play the tabla.”
items.hi: मेरी बेटी को तबला बजाना ___ है ।
items.say: मेरी बेटी को तबला बजाना आता है ।
items.en: My[0] daughter[1+2] can[5+6] play[4] the tabla[3].
wrong: The verb agrees with its subject, the infinitive बजाना, a masculine noun. बेटी has को and does not control the verb.
आते is plural. The subject is the infinitive, which is singular.
items.why: X को + infinitive + आना “X knows how to …”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My husband can't cook.”
items.hi: मेरे पति को खाना ___ नहीं आता है ।
items.say: मेरे पति को खाना बनाना नहीं आता है ।
items.en: My[0] husband[1+2] can't[5+6+7] cook[3+4].
wrong: As the subject of आना the infinitive is direct: बनाना.
बनाता is the imperfective participle. आना takes the infinitive.
items.why: The infinitive is the subject of आता है, so it stays direct.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I am going to phone my (own) brother right now. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: मैं अभी अपने भाई को फ़ोन ___ जा रहा हूँ ।
items.say: मैं अभी अपने भाई को फ़ोन करने जा रहा हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] {am going}[7+8+9] {to phone}[4+5+6] {my (own)}[2] brother[3] {right now}[1]. (a man speaking)
wrong: With जाना of purpose the infinitive is oblique: करने जा रहा हूँ.
करूँगा is the future, “I will do”; it cannot go before जा रहा हूँ.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + जा रहा हूँ “I'm going to …”, as in English.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Care is essential in driving a car.”
items.say: गाड़ी चलाने में सावधानी ज़रूरी है ।
items.en: Care[3] is[5] essential[4] in[2] driving[1] a car[0].
wrong: Before में the infinitive is oblique: चलाने में.
Not a word: the oblique infinitive ends in -ne, with no nasal.
items.why: The infinitive is also a masculine noun: direct as a subject (जाना), oblique in -e before a postposition or for purpose (जाने).

items.q: Why is it जाने in जाने से पहले?
items.a: जाने is the oblique infinitive: a masculine noun before a postposition
wrong: There is nothing plural here. -ne is the oblique singular, as in कमरे में.
Because जाने is the imperfective participle
The participle is जाता, जाते. जाने is the oblique of the infinitive जाना.
items.why: The infinitive is also a masculine noun: direct as a subject (जाना), oblique in -e before a postposition or for purpose (जाने).

items.en: {The girls}[0] {will go}[4] {to the market}[3] {in the evening}[1+2].
wrong: जाएँगे is masculine. लड़कियाँ is feminine.
जाएगी is singular. लड़कियाँ is plural.

items.en: I[0] {will give}[4] you[1] this[2] book[3]. (a woman speaking, to तुम)
wrong: Not a word: देना is irregular, दूँगी.
दूँगा is masculine. The speaker is a woman.

items.en: {At this time}[1+2] tomorrow[0] Sita[3] {will be working}[6+7+8+9] in[5] the office[4].
wrong: होगा is masculine. Sita is a woman.
रहा is masculine. Sita is a woman: कर रही होगी.

items.en: Mohan[0] {must be}[4] {at home}[2+3] now[1].
wrong: है states a fact: “Mohan is at home”. “Must be” is the future, होगा.
होगी is feminine. Mohan is a man.

items.en: We[0] {will meet}[3] {right here}[2] tomorrow[1].
wrong: यही is “this very one”. “Right here” is यहीं.

items.en: My[3] uncle[4+5] lives[6+7] in[2] {this very}[0] village[1].
wrong: यही is direct. Before में the phrase is oblique: इसी गाँव में.
चाचा जी takes plural agreement for respect: रहते हैं.

items.en: {There are}[6] many[3] new[4] shops[5] in[2] this[0] lane[1].
wrong: बहुत-से is masculine. दुकानें is feminine.
नए is masculine. दुकानें is feminine.

items.en: {Getting up}[1] {early in the morning}[0] is[3] good[2].
wrong: As a subject the infinitive is direct: उठना.
अच्छी is feminine. The infinitive is a masculine noun: अच्छा.

items.en: After[3+4] finishing[1+2] the work[0] we[5] {will go}[7] home[6].
wrong: Before के बाद the infinitive is oblique: करने.

items.en: Pinki[0] {is going}[6+7+8] to the station[5] to fetch[4] {her (own)}[1] brother[2+3].
wrong: For purpose the infinitive is oblique: लेने.
उसके would be someone else's brother. For the subject's own, use अपने.

items.en: Raj[0+1] {can sing}[2+3+4].
wrong: As the subject of आना the infinitive is direct: गाना.
The verb agrees with the infinitive गाना, which is masculine: आता.

items.en: Will you[0] take[2] tea[1] or[3] coffee[4]? (to a woman)
wrong: Not a word: लेना is irregular, लेगी, लेंगी.
लेंगे is masculine. This is asked of a woman.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: राज इस समय रेलगाड़ी में होगा ।
items.a: Raj must be on the train at the moment.
wrong: Raj was on the train at this time.
Past would be था. होगा with इस समय is an assumption about now.
Raj is on the train at the moment, I know.
है would state it as a fact. होगा is an assumption: “must be”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: “Too” would be भी. ही is “only, not until”.
अगले महीने is “next month”, and लौटेंगे is future.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: That would be बहुत अच्छे कपड़े. बहुत-से qualifies कपड़े — “many”.
-se after an adjective like महँगे would give “quite expensive”. बहुत-से is “many”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: इस गाँव का पानी पीने लायक़ नहीं है ।
items.a: The water of this village isn't fit to drink.
wrong: The water of this village isn't easy to drink.
“Easy” would be आसान. लायक़ is “worth, fit for”.
Nobody drinks the water of this village.
Nothing here says “nobody”. पीने लायक़ is “worth drinking, fit to drink”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरे छोटे भाई को साइकिल चलाना नहीं आता ।
items.a: My little brother can't ride a bicycle.
wrong: My little brother doesn't come by bicycle.
With an infinitive as subject, आना means “to know how to”.
My little brother doesn't like riding a bicycle.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: Before an adjective काफ़ी means “quite”. Nothing here is negative.
बड़ा is “big”, and काफ़ी is “quite”, not “very”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: इस कमरे में खाना खाना मना है ।
items.a: Eating is not allowed in this room.
wrong: Eat your food in this room.
A command would be खाओ. खाना खाना is the verbal noun “eating food”.
There is no food in this room.

items.q: Which three verbs have irregular futures?
wrong: These are regular: जाऊँगा, आएगा, करेंगे.
पीना and छूना only shorten their vowel: पिएगा, छुएगा.
items.why: होना, लेना and देना are irregular: हूँगा, होगा, होगे, होंगे — लूँगा, लेगी, लेंगे — दूँगा, देगा, देंगे.

items.q: Does the future tense use an auxiliary verb?
items.a: No: the future is one word, like बोलेगा
wrong: Yes: like the present, it adds है
The future needs no auxiliary: बोलेगा on its own is “will speak”.
Only in the negative, with नहीं
The negative is नहीं बोलेगा, still with no auxiliary.
items.why: The future adds -ū̃gā to the stem for मैं, -egā for तू, यह, वह, -oge for तुम and -ẽge for हम, आप, ये, वे. Feminine forms end in -ī: -ū̃gī, -egī, -ogī, -ẽgī.

items.q: What is the difference between यहीं and यही?
items.a: यहीं is “right here”, a place; यही is “this very one”
wrong: None: यहीं and यही are two spellings of one word
They are different words: यहाँ + ही gives यहीं, यह + ही gives यही.
Neither is plural. The nasal comes from यहाँ.
items.why: Likewise वहीं “right there” and वही “that very one”.

items.q: What does -sī add in लाल-सी?
wrong: -sā after बहुत gives “many”; after an adjective it gives “-ish”.
items.why: -sā agrees like an -ā adjective: लाल-सा, लाल-सी, लाल-से.

items.q: Does ही change the case of the word before it?
items.a: No: ही is not a postposition, so the word stays as it is
wrong: Yes: the word before ही becomes oblique
Only a postposition makes a word oblique. ही is like भी.
Yes: the word before ही becomes plural
ही has nothing to do with number.
items.why: ही emphasises or limits the word just before it, often “only”.

items.q: Which is the formal (Sanskrit-derived) word for “but”?
wrong: पर is the everyday short word for “but”.
items.why: Formal words: पुस्तक, कठिन, व्यवस्था, परंतु — everyday words: किताब, मुश्किल, इंतज़ाम, लेकिन.
